project.name: Herald.OSS Core Engine
project.description: The log-event hot path of Herald.OSS — an open-source, zero-allocation structured logging kernel for .NET 8/9/10. nodes.name: PriorityWindowSamplingFilter.cs
nodes.summary: Per-level priority sampler with a sliding-tumbling window guarantee.  Existing samplers ( 1-in-N, AdaptiveSamplingFilter) are global: they decide admission without caring which level the event carries. Under high-volume floods this hides the events operators care about most. Pin "always keep at least 60 error events per minute" with :   var sampler = new PriorityWindowSamplingFilter( minimumPerLevel: new Dictionary<LogLevel, int> { [KnownLogLevels.Error] = 60, [KnownLogLevels.Warn] = 200, }, windowDuration: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), defaultSampleRate: 1000);            // 1-in-1000 for everything else builder.WithSamplingFilter(sampler);   Per call, the filter advances the per-level window if the system clock crossed a boundary, then increments that level's counter. Events whose counter is at or below the configured minimum admit unconditionally; events past the minimum fall through to defaultSampleRate (1-in-N) sampling. Levels not present in the minimum map use the default rate from the first event.  Thread safety. Each level owns an isolated counter cell. Window rollover and increment use  against a packed (windowIndex, count) long, so concurrent callers across every level pay no contention with each other and contention within a single level reduces to a single CAS per event. No allocations on the hot path; the cells dictionary is read-only after construction. Edition. Community. Tests. tests/Filters/PriorityWindowSamplingFilterTests.cs. Part of the filter area: decides which log events proceed (level gating, sampling, throttling, escalation). Defines PriorityWindowSamplingFilter, LevelCell.

nodes.name: FileLineWriter.cs
nodes.summary: Append-only file writer backed by a long-lived .  Older revisions opened, appended, and closed the file on every  via  — three syscalls per event, plus the kernel-side path resolution. The stream stays open for the writer's lifetime under a  share so log-tailing tools (tail -f, the dashboard's live view, log shippers) can read concurrently. Writes call  without flushToDisk so bytes are visible to other readers right away — that matches the implicit guarantee callers got from File.AppendAllText. Durability-on-write is opt-in via the writeThrough constructor flag, which sets .   Disposal flushes pending bytes with flushToDisk: true and closes the stream. nodes.name: LineSanitizer.cs
nodes.summary: Escapes control characters in a log line before it is written to a text file sink. nodes.summary: Coordinates external-source registrations against a pipeline's sink gates. Holds the timestamp lock that prevents a rogue caller from re-registering an existing key under different terms, derives a new key from (referenceSource, rawKey, timestamp), and pushes the derived key into the named sinks' accepted-source lists. Hot reload. The registrar's snapshot is exposed via  so a downstream rebuild step can replay every active registration against the new sink gates via . Without that, a hot reload silently revokes every external source.   Architectural seam. Herald.OSS does not stamp GenSource on events through its default factories, and no OSS code path constructs a registrar by default. The registrar class is present so downstream commercial wrappers (or an OSS adopter that wants multi-tenant routing) can compose  gates with an HMAC-keyed registrar without re-implementing the timestamp lock, persistence boundary, or rebind contract. nodes.summary: File-backed implementation of . Persists the snapshot as JSON at a configured path. Atomic write via temp-file-plus-rename so a crash mid-write leaves the previous snapshot intact. nodes.name: HeraldHost.cs
nodes.summary: Aggregates the per-host registry surface that previously lived as process-wide static classes.  Why an instance form exists. Every JSON-kind registry was a public static class, which is the right pattern for a registry (lookup-by-name + factory dispatch) but the wrong pattern for test isolation and multi-tenant plugin scoping. Two parallel xUnit classes that each register the same custom kind would step on each other; a multi-tenant Enterprise host could not give tenant A a different enricher kind than tenant B.   Backward-compatible shape. The static classes still exist — every existing caller (Embed, Lean, Server, Sinks) keeps compiling without change. Each static method now forwards to HeraldHost.Default.<Registry>.<Method>. New code paths that want isolation construct their own  via new HeraldHost() and consume the instance properties directly.   The host owns kind-registries AND the named-pipeline registry. The static  facade now forwards to HeraldHost.Default.Pipelines, so a multi-tenant Enterprise scenario can construct one host per tenant and keep the (tenant, name) map fully isolated from other tenants. nodes.name: HeraldRegistry.cs
nodes.summary: Global registry of named Herald pipeline instances. Use this when your application has multiple pipelines (e.g., a game server that slots in a combat logger, an economy logger, and a network logger independently). Each pipeline can be created, retrieved, and removed by name.  Hosting model. The static surface forwards every call to 's . Tests and multi-tenant hosts that want isolation construct their own  and consume host.Pipelines directly. Existing single-host callers keep working unchanged through this facade.   Multi-tenancy is modeled as the default shape: every entry belongs to a tenant, and single-tenant callers fall through to . The back-compat overloads (no tenant argument) forward to the default tenant so existing code keeps working. Enterprise builds unlock additional tenants; other editions throw on non-default registration.  Thread-safe. All operations are safe to call from any thread. Usage: // Single-tenant (default tenant, unchanged behaviour) var builder = QuickLogBuilder.Create("combat") .WithFileSink("logs/combat.log"); var result = builder.Build(); HeraldRegistry.Register(builder, result); // Retrieve from anywhere var combat = HeraldRegistry.Get("combat"); // Multi-tenant (Enterprise) HeraldRegistry.Register("studio-a", builderA, resultA); HeraldRegistry.Register("studio-b", builderB, resultB); var fromStudioA = HeraldRegistry.Get("studio-a", "combat"); Part of the quick-builder area: the QuickLogBuilder fluent facade and HeraldRegistry that assemble a pipeline. nodes.name: QuickLogBuilder.FastPath.cs
nodes.summary: Install kernel-aware redaction. Rules run on the property span before the  is constructed and stay on the kernel fast path — they do not register as  instances and do not move the pipeline off the compact dispatch path.  Trade-off vs : the fast path supports only the exact-name + Remove / Mask / Hash subset of the rule API. Pattern rules (glob / regex), event-action rules (DropEvent / ReplaceMessage), and value-pattern conditions belong on the heavier ; passing them here throws at builder time. Most production redaction shapes are exact-name only, so this is the dominant case.   Both convenience methods can be combined when a pipeline has both a hot-path subset (handled here, kernel-eligible) and a long-tail subset (handled by , event-pipeline path). The two redactors run independently — fast first, processor second — but a pipeline that uses both is no longer kernel-eligible because the event processor disqualifies it. The fast redactor still runs in that mode, but the structural floor is paid anyway, so combining the two only makes sense when the long tail is genuinely required. tour.title: The Public Logging Surface
tour.description: Start where consumers start. ILogger is the contract every call site binds against; TypedLogger/TypedLoggerFactory give a category-typed facade. These are the entry types — everything below exists to serve a call to one of these.

tour.title: Assembling a Pipeline the Quick Way
tour.description: QuickLogBuilder is the fluent way to stand up logging without JSON files. It accumulates sinks, filters, enrichers, and steps, then feeds a config through the same bootstrap path the JSON route uses. HeraldRegistry/HeraldHost are the composition roots that hold the built pipeline.

tour.title: Bootstrap and Hot Reload
tour.description: The bootstrap factory reads a JSON config and composes the pipeline. HotReloadableLoggingBootstrap watches for config changes and recomposes the pipeline in place — the same compose boundary the Quick builder hits, so a reload rebuilds exactly what a cold start would.

tour.title: The Kernel Contract and the Stack Buffer
tour.description: This is the hot path. IKernelSink is the single contract every built-in sink implements. LogEventBuffer is a ref struct that lives on the caller’s stack — the kernel hands it straight to sinks with no heap LogEvent and no boxing. The ref-struct constraint is what keeps the accept path zero-allocation.

tour.title: Compiling and Adapting the Kernel
tour.description: KernelEligibility decides whether a pipeline can take the fast path; KernelCompiler emits the filter + fan-out work as a single method over the buffer so the JIT keeps it in registers. KernelBufferAdapter is the bridge that materializes a heap event only when a non-kernel sink actually needs one.

tour.title: The Decorator Pipeline
tour.description: When the kernel fast path does not apply, events flow through a chain of logger decorators. IPipelineStepHandler defines a step; the step-handler registry and BuiltInStepHandlers wire the ordered stages (filtering, batching, async, fan-out, processors) around the core.

tour.title: Deciding What Survives: Filters and Levels
tour.description: Before an event does any work, it has to pass the gate. The level registry and switches resolve the effective minimum level (globally and per category/context); FilteringLogger and the sampling/throttling filters drop or down-sample events the pipeline should not pay to render.

tour.title: Enriching the Event
tour.description: Enrichers attach contextual properties — correlation id, activity, machine/process/thread, exception detail — through the ILogEnricher contract. CompositeLogEnricher runs a set of them in order so the event carries full context by the time it is rendered.

tour.title: The Event Payload
tour.description: LogEvent is the immutable payload. The event factory keeps time access, scope capture, enrichment, and template rendering out of the rest of the pipeline; the deferred factory builds the event lazily so cost is only paid when an event actually proceeds.

tour.title: Rendering Output
tour.description: Once an event survives, the output area turns it into text. Transformers and theme/style resolvers shape a console line; the rolling file writer and confined-path resolver handle durable file output with rotation and a sandboxed path.

tour.title: Routing and Loopback
tour.description: Sink providers route rendered events to their destinations through the provider registry. The loopback path feeds events back to in-process consumers — an event bus, a file, or a URL poster — with per-sink run-state and runtime overrides so an operator can flip a sink without a rebuild.
